abstract.para: The topic focuses on the services that make up PCP, and how to enable and start them.

topic.para: Installing the pcp package installs several &systemd; services, all disabled by default:

listitem.para: The Performance Metrics Collector Daemon. It coordinates the gathering and exporting of performance statistics in response to requests from PCP tools, and is required by every other PCP service. By default, it listens only on the local host, on port 44321.
Records the metrics exported by pmcd to archive logs, by default under /var/log/pcp/pmlogger/HOSTNAME/.
Exposes a REST API (PMWEBAPI) to access metrics remotely, on port 44322 by default. Unlike pmcd, it listens on all interfaces by default.
The inference engine. It evaluates the exported metrics against a set of rules and can trigger an action, for example, an alert, when a rule matches.

topic.para: Enable and start the services you need with systemctl. A single enable --now call both starts the service immediately and keeps it running across reboots, so no separate step is needed to persist it. For example, to enable local metric collection and logging:
Add pmproxy or pmie to the same command if you need the REST API or the inference engine.

note.title: Enabling services on the immutable mode
note.para: Enabling and starting a service only writes to /etc, which remains writable through an overlay even on the immutable mode of &productnameshort;, so the command above works there too without going through &tr-up;. Run it after the reboot that activates a freshly installed pcp package, rather than chaining it together with the installation itself. A live /etc change made against the snapshot you are about to leave is not guaranteed to carry over to the new one.

topic.para: By default, pmcd only accepts connections from the local host, and &firewalld; does not open a port for either pmcd or pmproxy. If you need to reach either service from another system, open the corresponding port:
Use port 44321 for pmcd and 44322 for pmproxy. Allowing remote connections to pmcd also requires changing PMCD_LOCAL, as described in .
